summary: Re-tested live SkillMatch auth, volunteer dashboard heading, organizer management, event creation, certificate navigation, logout, and mobile rendering. UI flows passed; completion validation correctly rejects a nonexistent volunteer/event. Existing API regression tests were state-dependent and failed because the seeded event was already completed by earlier runs.

minor.issue: Successful login returns id as an empty string because the query projection excludes _id before public_user builds the response.
Returns {ok:true} even when no matching application exists; should validate matched_count and return 404/409.

action_items: Make API regression fixtures/state cleanup idempotent so completion tests do not depend on prior runs.
Return a real user id or omit id from public auth responses when _id is projected out.
Validate application matched_count in the organizer status update endpoint.
critical_code_review_comments: Completion matched_count guard is now effective: invalid completion returned 409 and did not falsely succeed.
Existing regression test mutates seeded event-python state, causing later runs to fail; isolate test data or assert current state before mutation.

success_rate.backend: 50% (2 regression tests failed due to persisted state)

seed_data_creation: Created one UI Test Event through organizer UI; no users or seeded records changed intentionally. Existing test suite had already completed event-python before this iteration.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Maya and campusadmin login, clean volunteer heading, certificates navigation, organizer manage view, create-event flow, logout, and 390px mobile rendering all passed. Re-run completion against isolated accepted and non-accepted applications.
rca of the issue: The two pytest failures are caused by persistent remote MongoDB state: the volunteer test expects event-python certificate 404, while a prior run completed it; the organizer test then expects accepted completion but receives 409 because the application is already completed. This is test contamination rather than a live completion-handler regression.
